cover.sub: From the first Tornado Cash withdrawal to the revocation 40 hours later, rebuilt from the Ethereum record and 53,181 posts across X, TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, Reddit and news.

exec.title: A rehearsed attack, a four-hour open door, and a crowd that rebuilt it before Binance spoke
exec.lead: On the evening of October 29, a wallet funded only through Tornado Cash attached its own code to Binance 14, one of the exchange's main Ethereum hot wallets, and swept it in a single transaction. Every step had been rehearsed on mainnet that afternoon. The attacker's code then stayed on the wallet for 3 hours 49 minutes. Stablecoin issuers froze what they could inside the first hour. Binance said at 00:13 UTC that it would cover all losses, and at 00:52 that about $3 billion was frozen.

findings.title: It was rehearsed in public
findings.body: The operator deployed its first sweeper at 02:28 UTC, then rehearsed twice on its own wallets: at 13:51, and at 16:20 the full sequence with the production contract. Delegate, sweep, leave 1 ETH, withdraw. All on mainnet, with the rehearsals starting 6 hours 29 minutes before the delegation.

findings.title: Fifty authorizations, one signing key
findings.body: At 20:20:59 a single transaction delivered 50 EIP-7702 authorizations, every one signed by Binance 14's own key. The one matching the wallet's live nonce applied. Three minutes later one sweep moved 167,464 ETH and 63 tokens for $0.93 in gas.

findings.title: The door stayed open for 3h 49m
findings.body: The attacker's code ran on Binance 14 until 00:10:35. In that window it pulled 823M USDC from a second wallet that trusted Binance 14, re-swept 200.4M USDT, and the wallet kept receiving transfers: 533 of them.

findings.title: Issuers moved before the exchange
findings.body: Tether's $971M freeze was on the feed at 21:05. Binance's first word came at 21:15, from CZ and the company in the same minute. Tether, Circle and World Liberty froze in sequence; Binance also thanked Ripple, though no freeze shows on the traced XRP account; it put the verified total at $2.54B at 23:22 and about $3B at 00:52.

findings.title: Social rebuilt every step
findings.body: The sweep was described publicly 8 minutes after it landed, and the contract and the fifty authorizations within the hour. The rehearsals were found at 21:31. The setup itself, visible on-chain for 18 hours, drew no post until the money was gone.

overview.title: The whole hack on one page
overview.lead: Six lanes, one clock. The left panel covers October 28 06:00 to October 29 20:00, when the setup ran; the right panel covers the five hours of the attack at about 9.5 times the scale.

acts.title: The setup
acts.headline: Eighteen hours from the first contract to the drain, all on a public chain, with no post about any of it
acts.dek: Everything the attack needed was built and tested in the open on October 28 and 29: funding, two contracts and two rehearsals, the second a full run.

steps.title: Funded through Tornado Cash
steps.body: Two 0.1 ETH withdrawals from the Tornado Cash pool reach the operator 0x7C86…5CA0, at 07:39 and 08:53; a third follows at 08:23 on Oct 29. Two sibling wallets, 0xFD41 and 0xe4F9, are funded the same way. About 1.49 ETH in total: the operation's entire budget.

steps.title: Sweeper v1 deployed
steps.body: The operator deploys its first sweeper contract, 0x19be…f2bf. It has never been verified on any explorer.

steps.title: Rehearsal one
steps.body: Two fresh wallets controlled by the operator are delegated to the sweeper with EIP-7702 transactions, seeded with a few dollars of USDT and USDC, and swept at 14:19 and 14:24.

steps.title: Sweeper v2 deployed
steps.body: The production contract, 0x63e8…6fAe. Only the operator can call it. Its sweep leaves exactly 1 ETH behind, and it has an execute passthrough and a withdraw function.

steps.title: Rehearsal two, the full sequence
steps.body: A third test wallet is delegated, funded with 1.01 ETH, swept at 16:30 (0.01 ETH out, 1 ETH left) and emptied with a withdraw call at 16:47. The exact sequence used on Binance 14 three and a half hours later.

steps.title: Funding for the real run
steps.body: 0xe4F9 sends the operator 1.082 ETH.

acts.title: The drain
acts.headline: One delegation, one sweep: 167,464 ETH and 63 tokens left Binance 14 for $0.93 in gas
acts.dek: The attack on Ethereum took 3 minutes 24 seconds from delegation to sweep. Within 40 minutes a second wallet had released 823M USDC to the same address.

steps.title: $331M of outflows on two other chains
steps.body: 185,017,485 XRP ($236M) leaves Binance-labeled accounts for a new XRP Ledger account at 20:05, and 965,455 SOL ($95M) moves to a new Solana address at 20:10. Whale Alert labels the senders as Binance; Binance has not said whether these were its own transfers.

steps.title: The delegation
steps.body: One transaction from the operator to Binance 14 (0x28C6…1d60) carries 50 EIP-7702 authorizations. All 50 recover to Binance 14's own key. The one matching the wallet's live nonce, 18914809, applies; Binance 14's next transaction uses 18914810. The wallet now runs the attacker's code.

steps.title: The sweep
steps.body: One call moves 167,464 ETH and 63 tokens to 0x5227…2f8c, later labeled Binance Hot Wallet Exploiter 2. The largest lines: 1.615B USDT, 62.6M RLUSD, 29,934 wBETH, 11,372 XAUt. Gas: 0.000414 ETH, about $0.93.

steps.title: 780M USDC through a trusted wallet
steps.body: Using the execute passthrough, a call leaves Binance 14 to Hot Wallet 34 (0xEe7a…), a proxy that accepts Binance 14 as its owner. It releases 780M USDC to 0x5227.

steps.title: 43M USDC more
steps.body: The same route releases another 43M USDC.

acts.title: The open door
acts.headline: For 3 hours 49 minutes the wallet ran the attacker's code and kept receiving funds
acts.dek: Each sweep left exactly 1 ETH, enough for Binance 14 to keep paying for its own transactions. It kept transacting, kept looking normal, and kept taking in transfers.

steps.title: Transfers keep arriving
steps.body: Blockscout records 533 incoming token transfers to Binance 14 while it is delegated, including 205.7M USDT, 180B PEPE and 859M SHIB. Its own transactions run from nonce 18914810 to 18914903: the key holder is still transacting throughout.

steps.title: First re-sweep
steps.body: 3.9M USDT plus dust.

steps.title: Second re-sweep
steps.body: 200.4M USDT, 6,591 LINK, 7,008 UNI and smaller lines.

steps.title: The long tail
steps.body: A basket of smaller tokens, worth at least $7.5M on the ten largest lines the explorer lists, goes to a second receiver, 0xA97b….

steps.title: Six empty sweeps
steps.body: Between 23:36 and 23:56 the operator calls sweep six more times. Nothing moves.

steps.title: Revocation
steps.body: Binance 14 signs its own type-4 (EIP-7702) transaction pointing its delegation at the zero address, clearing the attacker's code 3 hours 49 minutes after it landed. Binance 14's own outgoing transfers between 00:47 and 01:53 fail.

acts.title: The response
acts.headline: The issuers froze first; Binance's verified frozen total reached about $3 billion by 00:52
acts.dek: Tether's first freeze reached the feed ten minutes before any Binance account spoke. Over the next four hours, issuers froze in sequence and Binance moved from holding statements to a full pause.

steps.title: Tether freezes $971M
steps.body: First reported by @TreeNewsFeed: 'Tether freezes $971M USDT in likely Binance hack, with no update from Binance still.'

steps.title: Circle freezes 823M USDC
steps.body: Jeremy Allaire confirms more than 800M USDC frozen at 21:18, in coordination with law enforcement (per The Block).

steps.title: CZ: 'It does look like a hack'
steps.body: 'User funds are safe! It does look like a hack on Binance. Appreciate the quick freeze from Tether (~$971m) and Circle (~$823m).' The most-engaged post of the event. @binance posts three holding statements at 21:15, 21:16 and 21:24.

steps.title: Tether raises its freeze to 1.567B USDT
steps.body: Paolo Ardoino: 'Tether froze more than 1.567B USDT related to a potential Binance exchange hack.'

steps.title: 'User funds are completely safe'
steps.body: @binance reposts its statement with one added sentence. It draws ten times the engagement of the versions without it.

steps.title: Aave freezes its USDT market
steps.body: Aave freezes its USDT market, blocking new borrowing against it, per @WatcherGuru.

steps.title: Binance thanks Ripple; World Liberty freezes
steps.body: Yi He thanks Ripple for freezing 'approximately 200 million' (unit not stated; no freeze shows on the traced XRP account), and at 22:22 World Liberty Financial for $27M USD1 and 48M WLFI.

steps.title: 'Will cover'
steps.body: CZ, replying to a net-loss estimate of about $1B: 'Loss might be a bit higher than that, but will cover.'

steps.title: Some withdrawals processed
steps.body: Per CryptoTicker, some BTC, ETH and USDT withdrawals were being processed at 22:32; Binance's 22:33 notice said withdrawals would resume once the issue was resolved. Binance Alpha trading is suspended at 23:06.

steps.title: $2.54B verified frozen
steps.body: Binance addresses 'differing figures circulating publicly' and puts the verified frozen total at $2.54B.

steps.title: Full pause; about $3B frozen
steps.body: 'Binance will cover all losses. As a precaution, all deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended.' At 00:52: 'The current verified total frozen amount is around $3 billion.'

acts.title: The public record
acts.headline: Each step of the drain was public within about an hour; the setup waited 5 to 37 hours
acts.dek: Independent analysts reconstructed the attack from the chain in real time. The record they built is the spine of this report.
body: The sweep was public in 8 minutes and the 780M USDC pull in 7. By 21:25, about an hour after the delegation, posts had the mechanism, the contract, the hardcoded operator and the fifty authorizations, and every one of those claims checks out against the chain.

The setup was a different story. The first sweeper sat on-chain for 19 hours before anyone wrote about it, and both rehearsals were found only after the money had moved. The same pattern, a mixer-funded address delegating test wallets to unverified code and sweeping them, was visible from 13:51.

What varied across posts was never the sequence. It was the total: reported outflow estimates ran from $2.53B at 20:39 to $5.57B by 21:12, and $5.7B by 21:58, depending on which chains and which freezes were counted.
